subject: general
question: As per the treaty of Purandar, how many forts were surrendered by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj to Mughals?
solution:
The correct answer is __**23**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Treaty of Purandar, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj agreed to surrender 23 forts to the Mughal Empire.
 
• This treaty was signed on June 11, 1665, between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and Raja Jai Singh I, who was representing the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.
 
• The forts surrendered included strategically significant ones like Purandar, Rudramal, Lohgad, and Mahuli.
 
• The treaty also required Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj to pay a compensation of 400,000 huns to the Mughal Empire.
 
• In return, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was allowed to retain 12 forts along with an area worth an annual income of 100,000 huns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Treaty of Purandar (1665)**: This was a pivotal agreement between the Maratha ruler Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and the Mughal Empire, marking a temporary halt in hostilities.
 
• **Raja Jai Singh I**: He was a Rajput general serving under Emperor Aurangzeb, who played a key role in negotiating the Treaty of Purandar with Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.
 
• **Forts**: These were crucial military assets in medieval India, often serving as administrative centers and military strongholds.
 
• **Compensation Payment**: The payment of 400,000 huns by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj to the Mughals was a significant financial burden, reflecting the substantial economic costs of the treaty.
 
• **Strategic Retreat**: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj's decision to surrender the forts was seen as a strategic retreat to buy time and consolidate his forces for future resistance against the Mughals.
